title: Reading a bitmap header
description:
BMP image files start with a header. Write `readBmpHeader(buffer)` that takes an `ArrayBuffer` and returns `{ fileSize, dataOffset, width, height, topDown, bitsPerPixel }`, using a `DataView` (every value is little-endian):

| offset | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 bytes | the letters `BM` |
| 2 | uint32 | file size |
| 10 | uint32 | where the pixel data starts |
| 14 | uint32 | header size, at least 40 |
| 18 | int32 | width |
| 22 | int32 | height: negative means the rows are stored top-down |
| 26 | uint16 | planes, must be 1 |
| 28 | uint16 | bits per pixel: 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 or 32 |

Return `height` as a positive number and `topDown` as a boolean. Throw an `Error` when the buffer is shorter than 54 bytes, the letters are wrong, the header size is under 40, the planes are not 1, the bits are not allowed, or the width is 0 or less.
hints: Every `DataView` getter takes `true` as its second argument here, for little-endian: `view.getUint32(2, true)` (lesson 8.01).
Check the length first: reading past the end of a `DataView` throws a `RangeError`, which is not the clear message you want.
